title: Transpose a matrix
statementMd: Return the transpose of a rectangular matrix (a list of rows): row `i` of the result is column `i` of the input. An empty matrix transposes to `[]`.
hints: A nested comprehension: `[[row[i] for row in matrix] for i in range(...)]`. Or try `zip(*matrix)`.
solutionMd:
```python
def transpose(matrix):
    if not matrix:
        return []
    return [[row[i] for row in matrix] for i in range(len(matrix[0]))]
```

The outer comprehension picks a column index, the inner one collects that column from every row. `[list(c) for c in zip(*matrix)]` is equivalent.
